Bowhill Engineering is seeking a motivated and detail-focused Project Assistant to join our team and support the delivery of major infrastructure projects through advanced digital

Specialising in large government infrastructure projects and complexity done excellently, Bowhill Engineering is powered by technology and driven by great people to optimise and build structures that matter.


About the Role
The Project Assistant plays a key role in strengthening quality, certainty and production flow by embedding advanced digital tools into everyday workshop and project execution. Working closely with Project, Production and Quality teams, you will support digital QA systems, production readiness, reporting and continuous improvement initiatives across the business. Through real-time data, visual verification and disciplined systems, you will help ensure fabrication is built right the first time while reducing rework and improving communication between teams. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys problem solving, technology, organisation and process improvement, while working in a fast-paced fabrication and manufacturing environment.


Key Responsibilities & Requirements
-Support and maintain digital QA systems including FabStation and HoloLens AR
-Assist with production readiness, work packs and planning coordination
-Ensure real-time production and QA data is accurate and up to date
-Support workshop teams with clear and accessible project information
-Monitor planned versus actual production performance and reporting
-Assist with compliance tracking, reporting and system updates
-Identify opportunities for improvement and help implement smarter processes
-Work collaboratively across Project, Production and Quality teams
-Help strengthen transparency, communication and workflow efficiency across projects
-Support continuous improvement initiatives and maintain OFI registers

Experience & Qualifications
-Current Driver’s Licence (Manual)
-Experience in steel fabrication, construction or manufacturing environments (desirable)
-Strong organisational and time management skills
-Excellent written and verbal communication skills
-Competent IT skills including MS Word, Excel & Outlook
-Experience with production software, Tekla or MS Project (desirable)
-Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings
-Strong attention to detail and problem-solving ability
-Understanding of WHS requirements and safe work practices

What We Offer
-Opportunity to work on major infrastructure projects of national significance
-Exposure to advanced digital fabrication and QA technology
-Career growth opportunities into a Production Systems Analyst role
-Supportive and collaborative team environment
-Employee Assistance Program (EAP)Employee Health Assistance
-Active Social Club and strong workplace culture
-Modern workplace with multiple workshops on site
-Enjoy the River Murray lifestyle
-Join an Employer of Choice in the Murraylands

About Us
Based in Bowhill, South Australia (90 mins from Adelaide, 40 mins from Murray Bridge, 30 mins from Mannum), Bowhill Engineering has built a national reputation for delivering large, complex steel structures with precision and pride — all from one location.
Apply Now - Bring your confidence in new technology & software, your analytical skills, quality focus & ability to capture, interpret & measure production data - we have an immediate spot waiting for you!
Submit your cover letter, resume, and three references via the Bowhill Engineering website.
For more information, contact HR Manager, Samantha Krollig on (08) 8570 4208.

FORMWORK CARPENTER 
KWIK FORMWORK
JANDAKOT, PERTH WA 6164 
FULL-TIME PERMANENT

Position Overview
As a Formwork Carpenter at KWIK FORMWORK, you will play a pivotal role in the construction, erection, and installation of formwork for various structures on key projects. This position requires a skilled tradesperson with leadership abilities to ensure the successful completion of tasks while maintaining high standards of safety and quality.

Key Responsibilities
•	Review and Interpret Plans: Carefully review and interpret project plans and blueprints to identify the materials needed, dimensions, and the best installation approach.
•	Material Selection and Planning: Select and order the necessary materials and prepare detailed layouts for the formwork construction process.
•	Construct, Erect, and Install Formwork: Execute precise measurements and work from technical drawings to create and set up formwork for concrete structures.
•	Installation of Cladding and Fixtures: Install fascia panels, roof sheathing, and fit exterior cladding, along with door and window frames, to complete the formwork.
•	Maintenance and Repairs: Carry out repairs on existing formwork and structures as needed, ensuring they remain functional and up to standard.
•	Versatile Material Handling: Work with a range of materials, including laminates, Perspex, and metals, as required by the project.
•	Lead and Supervise: Oversee a team of formwork carpenters, ensuring tasks are completed efficiently and to a high standard.
•	Safety Compliance: Adhere to and enforce safety protocols on-site, ensuring a safe working environment for all team members.
•	Quality Control: Inspect and verify the quality of the formwork installation, ensuring it meets project specifications and industry standards.
•	Collaboration: Work closely with project managers, engineers, and other trades to coordinate and streamline the construction process.
•	Problem-Solving: Identify and address any issues that arise during the formwork installation process, finding effective solutions to keep the project on track.
•	Training and Mentoring: Provide guidance and training to less experienced team members, fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

Qualifications and Skills
•	Cert III Equivalent & Experience: This position requires a Certificate III equivalent or a minimum of 3 years’ experience in the trade.
•	Industry Knowledge: Demonstrated industry knowledge is essential for this position.
•	WA Building and Construction Industry Card: A current WA Building and Construction Industry White/Blue Card is mandatory.
•	Technical Proficiency: Ability to read and interpret drawings accurately.
•	High-Rise Experience: Prior experience in high-rise construction is highly desirable.

The Client: 

Adio Desk Pty Ltd is an Australian provider of advanced telecommunications solutions, specialising in offering innovative and reliable telecommunications services.  

They now seek a skilled and qualified Telecommunication Network Planner to join their team in Bendigo in VIC on a full-time basis.  

 

 

The Role: 

This is for five (5) full time positions with an annual salary between $79,500 to $88,000 depending on experience plus superannuation. The role will be based in Bendigo in VIC. 

 

? 

The Responsibilities: 

Develop detailed telecommunications network plans including fibre, copper and wireless topology layouts 

Conduct capacity forecasting and traffic modelling to ensure network scalability and performance optimisation 

Design fibre optic routing plans including splice schematics, cable schedules and distribution architecture 

Perform radio frequency planning, propagation analysis and site configuration for wireless network deployments 

Prepare technical feasibility studies and cost estimation models for new infrastructure projects 

Liaise with engineers, field technicians, contractors and local authorities to coordinate infrastructure rollout 

Analyse network performance data to identify congestion points and recommend optimisation strategies 

Ensure network design compliance with ACMA regulations, Australian Standards and carrier specific requirements 

Develop GIS based mapping documentation and maintain accurate network asset records 

Review and validate contractor submissions, as built documentation and network acceptance reports 

Assess risk factors including environmental, zoning and technical constraints impacting network deployment 

Support commissioning and integration of new network segments into live environments 

Prepare technical reports, design documentation and stakeholder presentations for project approval 

Monitor emerging telecommunications technologies and recommend upgrades to maintain competitive capability  

 

 

The Requirements: 

At least a Diploma qualification in Telecommunications or a related field 

Minimum 1 year full time post qualification experience as a Telecommunications Network Planner  

At least 1 year experience in fibre optic network planning including route selection, splice planning and optical power budgeting 

Minimum 1 year experience conducting RF planning, coverage modelling and spectrum analysis for wireless deployments 

At least 1 year experience using GIS platforms, AutoCAD, RF planning tools or equivalent network design software 

At least 1 year experience ensuring compliance with ACMA regulations and carrier grade technical standards 

Minimum 1 year experience preparing structured technical documentation, feasibility studies and cost modelling for telecommunications infrastructure projects 

Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to perform on-site analysis and resolution of technical problems 

Ability to work independently and as part of a team 

Familiarity with maintaining detailed logs and documentation of inventories, parts, equipment, and instruments, as well as communication policies and procedures 

Ability to liaise effectively with vendors, suppliers, service providers, and external resources to monitor contractual obligations and performance delivery

You will contribute to teaching across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, wargaming, offensive and defensive security, and related cybersecurity disciplines at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. You will play a key role in delivering engaging learning experiences, developing innovative curriculum and teaching approaches, and enhancing student learning outcomes.

With established strengths in cybersecurity, systems, artificial intelligence, and software engineering, UNSW offers an exceptional environment for educators who are passionate about teaching excellence, curriculum innovation, and student success. You will contribute to a collaborative academic community committed to advancing education and preparing students for real-world impact.

This is an opportunity to join a global leader in Computer Science, with cutting-edge facilities, world-class faculty, and an innovative educational environment. With strong industry partnerships and a commitment to educational excellence, UNSW provides excellent opportunities for career development, collaboration, and impact.

About You
You are an engaging and passionate educator with expertise in cybersecurity and a commitment to delivering high-quality teaching and learning experiences. You bring knowledge in areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, wargaming, and offensive and defensive security, along with the ability to contribute to an inclusive and high-performing academic environment.

At Lecturer level (Level B), you will contribute to teaching, curriculum development, and student support across undergraduate and postgraduate courses, while continuing to develop your teaching practice and educational innovation capabilities.

At Senior Lecturer level (Level C), you will demonstrate educational leadership through curriculum innovation, mentoring colleagues, leading teaching initiatives, and contributing to the advancement of teaching excellence across the School and broader UNSW Education Focused community.
You are collaborative, adaptable, and motivated to create meaningful learning experiences while building strong relationships across academia and industry.

About UNSW
UNSW is a world leading institution recognised for its scale, prestige, and impact. With strong industry engagement and partnerships across sectors, UNSW provides a unique environment where academic expertise translates into real world outcomes. The university is home to cutting edge research that drives innovation and societal progress, while its excellence in teaching ensures students are prepared to lead in their fields. For academics, UNSW offers an outstanding platform to flourish — combining world class facilities, collaborative networks, and a culture of innovation that supports both career growth and meaningful contributions to the wider community.

The School of Computer Science and Engineering is one of the largest and most prestigious schools of computing in Australia. It offers undergraduate programmes in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, and Bioinformatics, as well as a number of combined degrees with other disciplines. Our research and teaching staff are world leading and world building as they advance knowledge and learning. For more information on our school, please visit: https://www.unsw.edu.au/engineering/our-schools/computer-science-and-engineering

•	A PhD in a related discipline, and/or relevant work experience.
•	Actively stays up to date with discipline knowledge and professional development.

•	Experience using and/or designing with educational technologies and online delivery methods.
•	Evidence of teaching effectiveness and passion for educational excellence (e.g. relevant discipline-based curriculum design and development at a variety of levels and scales).
•	Demonstrated knowledge of industry or experience in work-integrated learning (desirable).
•	Evidence of highly developed interpersonal and organisational skills.
•	Evidence of ability to support and inspire students from diverse backgrounds and support student equity, diversity and inclusion initiatives.
•	An understanding of and commitment to UNSW’s aims, objectives and values in action, together with relevant policies and guidelines.

Senior Lecturer (Level C)
•	A PhD in a related discipline, and/or relevant work experience.
•	Actively stays up to date with discipline knowledge and development.
•	Demonstrated experience in teaching and learning design using a range of pedagogical approaches, development and delivery of courses and programs, at undergraduate and/or postgraduate level. 
•	Experience in implementing educational technologies and online delivery methods.
•	Evidence of teaching effectiveness and passion for educational excellence and fostering this in others.
•	Demonstrated experience with industry or work-integrated learning. 
•	Evidence of professional development of teaching practice in self and others with the ability to advance and lead an inclusive culture of excellence in learning and teaching.
•	Demonstrated success in initiating curriculum development and improvement.
•	Evidence of highly developed interpersonal and organisational skills.
•	Evidence of ability to support and inspire students from diverse backgrounds and support student equity diversity and inclusion initiatives.
•	Demonstrated ability to interact with the profession and industry and attract funding for learning and teaching initiatives.
•	An understanding of and commitment to UNSW’s aims, objectives and values in action, together with relevant policies and guidelines.
•	Knowledge of health and safety responsibilities and commitment to attending relevant health and safety training.
